body.target_estimand:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\) and a labelled causal point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\), the causal target is
\[
 \tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s
 \mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}[B_{si}(1)-B_{si}(0)].
\]
For a joint panel law \(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}\), the corresponding conditional target \(\tau(z_0)\) and its identification are asserted only for almost every query under the marginal query law of \(P\).
body.estimand_functional:
At a fixed admissible query \(z_0\), every member of \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is a labelled point \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) on the common observable sigma-field \(\mathcal O\), and
\[
 \theta_{\mathrm{ker}}(\xi;z_0)
 =\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mu_s-m_s(z_{0s})\},
 \qquad
 \mu_s=\mathbb E_{\mathbb K_\xi}B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}.
\]
The lower design-density bound identifies every conditional regression \(m_s\) Lebesgue-almost everywhere, and Holder continuity uniquely extends that version to \(z_{0s}\); hence \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}\) is an observed-law functional.  Consistency and event-date transport, rather than this definition, imply \(\theta_{\mathrm{ker}}=\tau(z_0)\).  Every estimator and interval is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule chosen before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), with no access to potential outcomes or nuisance labels.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the deterministic fixed-design experiment gives the conditional optimal-recovery bound, and the random-design mean-squared-error and honest expected-length frontiers are uniform over the labelled fixed-query class.  The marginal squared-risk scale is \(R_\star=R_{\mathrm{or}}\vee N^{-\lambda}\), with the independent-calendar spacing replacement on \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm{iid}}_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\).  For each joint panel law, the labelled regular conditional point belongs to the fixed-query class and the conclusions transfer only for marginal-almost-every query.  No null conditional version, lower local modulus, calendar-score branch, or headline result for \(\lambda>1\) is used.

sampling_model.design: At each fixed admissible query, the statistical model consists of labelled points \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\) whose observable restriction is on \(\mathcal O=\sigma((X_{st}),(Q_{sti}),(B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}),(Z_j))\).  Each exact pre-event path has a density between \(c_X\) and \(C_X\) Lebesgue-almost-everywhere, and each cohort design sequence is geometrically beta mixing.  The independent-calendar subclass imposes independence only on the design dates.  Every decision rule is chosen before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\).
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks at every date and \(n_s\) treated event observations with common observed mean \(\mu_s\).  Conditional on the exact design, histories are independent across units, while dependence across all dates and the event outcome inside one unit history remains unrestricted.  Sampling concentration treats the complete history as one bounded observation.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency identifies observed event wealth with treated potential wealth.  Event-date transport separately equates the unobserved untreated event mean with the historical regression at the realized path.  These labelled causal clauses imply equality between the causal target and the observed-law functional; neither density positivity nor design centering proves transport.
sampling_model.overlap: Every admitted fixed query lies at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary.  Density positivity identifies a conditional regression Lebesgue-almost-everywhere, and Holder continuity then uniquely determines its value at the query.  Exact-site recovery can be easier than an anchor certificate; the regular donor converse additionally needs \(\delta_0<1/2\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated.  Donor folds provide projected means, and the full stacked covariance retains every cross-coordinate, cross-horizon, and cross-cohort covariance.  Nuisance labels index the model but are unavailable to estimators and intervals.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nonnegative local-constant weights allow whole-unit concentration without response mixing, deconvolution, calendar-score studentization, or division by an estimated variance.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Gaussian convex-class theory links linear-functional minimax risk to a known-experiment modulus; it does not supply the bounded replicated-response and generated-query product experiment used here.
Its estimated-minimizer results use sample splitting and strong convexity, making location error second order rather than a rough-Holder external-query modulus.
Its generated-covariate expansion attaches an estimated coordinate to every training row, unlike the exact historical design and generated event query here.
Its replicated errors-in-variables experiment contaminates every latent training coordinate and requires deconvolution, which is absent under center-only generation.
The classical random-design Holder benchmark supplies ordinary smoothing context but not query-conditional spacing or a generated donor center.
Pointwise local-polynomial minimax theory motivates the anchor smoother but not the bounded product-experiment nearest-site frontier.
Optimal local-polynomial kernels concern ordinary pointwise asymptotic efficiency; the present result establishes only rate constants for a generated-query product experiment.
Random-design sup-norm sharp estimation addresses global loss and design adaptation, not conditional nearest-site recovery at an external generated query.
Classical nonparametric errors-in-variables contaminates all regression covariates, so its deconvolution rates do not govern the center-only design used here.
Generated-regressor asymptotic variance uses smooth semiparametric expansions; it does not cover the nonsmooth rough-Holder query modulus or its minimax converse.
Honest confidence-interval adaptation impossibility motivates fixing the Holder radius and smoothness rather than claiming adaptation across classes.
Ordered moduli characterize confidence intervals for linear functionals in known Gaussian experiments; the current interval must additionally cover generated-center error.
Bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals combine worst-case bias and stochastic calibration but contain no external full-covariance donor query.
Dependent-data resampling is not invoked: the repaired theorem uses whole-unit bounded-range concentration and design mixing only for anchor occupancy.
Many-control panel asymptotics motivate cross-unit replication but do not provide the generated-query optimal-recovery frontier.
Dependent synthetic-control prediction intervals address dependent innovations and estimated weights; the repaired interval instead uses unit-history concentration and no calendar-block calibration.
Conformal synthetic-control inference targets robust prediction coverage under a different exchangeability/time-series architecture, not full-covariance generated-query expected-length minimaxity.
The synthetic-control review motivates consistency and data-architecture transparency but does not validate the event-date counterfactual transport equality used for causal identification.
The longitudinal and panel causal-model survey locates the identifying assumptions; it does not derive the conditional generated-proxy minimax or honest-length frontier.

body.tldr: The paper delivers a fixed-query minimax and honest-length frontier for the rough Holder regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), where \(\kappa=\lambda\).  Each point in \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) is explicitly labelled as \(\xi=(\mathbb K_\xi;\mu,m,\Sigma)\), but every estimator and interval is one \(\mathcal O\)-measurable rule selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), with no access to potential outcomes or nuisance labels.  The treated mean is observed, and design-density positivity plus Holder continuity makes \(m_s(z_{0s})\) unique under the observed law.  Consistency and the untestable event-date transport equality then identify the cohort-weighted buy-and-hold contrast.  The nonredundant rate channels are treated replication, query-conditional calendar spacing, and full-covariance donor location.  Conditional design independence removes the geometric-mixing logarithm; higher smoothness, uniform-in-query bands, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical fixed-point regression does not combine replicated sites with an external full-covariance generated query, and a panel regular conditional law is only determined marginal-almost-everywhere in that query.  Without an explicit observable sigma-field and labelled-parameter convention, a minimax display can also accidentally admit a query- or nuisance-dependent oracle rule.
project_justification.niche: Historical paths can be observed exactly while only the event-date counterfactual path is synthesized from donors.  A labelled fixed-query class separates the law available to the decision rule from nuisance labels used to index the model, while an almost-everywhere bridge keeps the causal panel interpretation version invariant.
project_justification.fill: The note defines \(\mathcal M_{N,T,\mathbf n}(z_0)\) as labelled points on one observable sigma-field \(\mathcal O\), proves that \(\mu_s\) and \(m_s(z_{0s})\) are observed-law functionals, and restricts every competitor to one observable-data rule chosen before the query and label.  For \(0<\lambda\le1\), nearest-site and anchor/extrapolation estimators attain the conditional and marginal risk rates, while a whole-unit bounded-range interval attains the honest expected-length rate.  Treated, clustered-spacing, and overlapping donor pairs give matching converses, and causal equality is proved separately from consistency and event-date transport.

body.related_work: Donoho (1994) relates a linear-functional modulus to minimax recovery in a known Gaussian convex experiment; the conditional theorem here instead constructs a bounded treated-response-donor product experiment with an external full-covariance query, a nearest-site characterization, an observable-only decision class, and a separate marginal-almost-everywhere causal bridge.  Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) study independently estimated minimizers under strong convexity, where center error is second order rather than a rough-Holder donor modulus.  Stone (1982), Fan (1993), Fan et al. (1997), and Gaiffas (2007) provide ordinary Holder, pointwise local-polynomial, kernel-efficiency, and random-design benchmarks; none supplies this labelled fixed-query replicated-panel frontier.  Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012), Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008), and Fan and Truong (1993) perturb training coordinates, unlike the exact historical design here; Hahn and Ridder (2013) gives smooth generated-regressor expansions rather than this nonsmooth location modulus.  Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) provide ordered-modulus and bias-aware ordinary-regression intervals, while Low (1997) motivates fixing the smoothness class.  Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021), Kunsch (1989), and Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu (2021) concern dependent prediction, resampling, or conformal architectures; the present interval instead concentrates independent whole-unit histories and uses no calendar calibration.  Ferman (2021) motivates many-control replication, while Abadie (2021) and Arkhangelsky and Imbens (2024) frame panel causal assumptions; none validates event-date transport or supplies the fixed-query statistical frontier.
body.interpretation: The labels \(\mu,m,\Sigma\) specify which member of the fixed-query model generated the data, but they are not inputs to the estimator or interval.  The observable law determines \(\mu_s\) directly and determines \(m_s(z_{0s})\) through density positivity and Holder continuity.  Donor uncertainty dominates when \(N^{-\lambda}\) exceeds treated replication and conditional spacing.  For a causal panel law, the statistical conclusions and the consistency-plus-transport identification step apply only at marginal-almost-every realized query.  Inference requires no calendar response mixing because it conditions on design and donors and concentrates across independent unit histories.
body.technical_internal_limitation: Every constructive headline is restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\), fixed admissible queries, and observable-data rules selected before the query and labelled parameter point.  Panel-law statements hold only marginal-almost-everywhere and are not uniform-in-query bands.  For \(\lambda>1\), signed higher-order weights lack the required whole-history stochastic-norm control.  Geometric conditional design mixing retains a logarithmic spacing penalty; only conditional design independence removes it.  The donor converse needs \(B^4>(Sd)^2\) and \(\delta_0<1/2\).  The total interval is rate-optimal but conservative, and exact phase-intersection constants remain open.
body.honest_scope: The fixed-query class is a labelled statistical model, not an oracle decision problem: every estimator and interval is \(\mathcal O\)-measurable, is selected before \(z_0\) and \(\xi\), and cannot inspect potential outcomes or \(\mu,m,\Sigma\).  Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction.  Query-conditional density and design mixing are observed-law restrictions, while design-conditional centering is a separate response restriction.  Donor-panel separation factors donors from the complete joint panel and permits arbitrary temporal dependence within a unit history.  Risk, coverage, and expected length are uniform over labelled points at a fixed query; each panel law inherits them only for marginal-almost-every query.  Higher smoothness, growing dimension, adaptation, uniform-in-query bands, and exact constants are outside scope.
